title: Validate Before Applying Effects
concept: Check declared and actual request size

writing.summary: Check declared and actual request size.
writing.rule: A body-length mismatch is a framing error; an exceeded limit is a resource error.
writing.explanation:
A request can advertise one size and deliver another. A server needs limits on both the declared size and accumulated bytes. Check limits before parsing the domain object or applying writes, otherwise an oversized request can consume unbounded resources or leave partial state.

This function receives an optional parsed Content-Length, actual byte count and maximum. Return 413 if either known size exceeds the maximum. Otherwise a present length that differs from actual input returns 400; valid bounded input returns 200. Missing length is accepted by this isolated policy when transport framing has already supplied a complete body. The native HTTP adapter has a stricter framing profile: it rejects chunked transfer, duplicate lengths and pipelined bytes. Never use this size-only policy as a complete HTTP parser.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Use curl -i -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @request.json http://127.0.0.1:8080/tasks and compare a rejected oversized title with a valid request.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.

writing.task: Return 413 if declared or actual bytes exceed maximum; otherwise 400 for a present mismatching length; otherwise 200. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: Can a small declared length replace a limit on actual bytes?
answers: No, actual bytes also need a bound
Yes, clients always report an accurate size
writing.feedback: Clients can lie or disconnect mid-body, so declared size alone is insufficient.

depth.misconception: Yes, clients always report an accurate size
depth.correction: A body-length mismatch is a framing error; an exceeded limit is a resource error.
